title: Five bottom-right utility patterns for SystemSketch
brief: Move the persistent SystemSketch release card off the top of the canvas and place its information behind Help, while adding familiar bottom-right zoom controls and a launcher for a placeholder right-side board panel. Copy proven Miro and FigJam interaction patterns and keep the tldraw integration narrow.
defaultWhy: FigJam Utility Strip is the provisional default at 92/100. It most directly follows the note's Figma-first decision, keeps every control visible in one familiar cluster, and gives the future panel a stable launcher. Its cost is one deliberately owned navigation component.
decisionHinge: The recommendation hinges on discoverability versus smallest implementation delta. Moving 10 weight points from Discoverable controls to Minimal custom code makes V1 and V2 tie at 88/100; if preserving more of tldraw's existing navigation structure dominates, choose Miro Satellites.
invariants: The canvas has no persistent SystemSketch version pill or release card at the top.
Help exposes the existing Stable/Preview status, version, build, release time, safety, changes, and release actions.
Zoom out, current zoom, zoom in, Help, and a placeholder right-side board panel remain reachable.
Use the same light dotted whiteboard, 27% zoom, status content, and 720 × 400 comparison viewport.
Keep the tldraw editor, tools, document model, and keyboard behavior intact.
boundary: These are self-contained interactive UI sketches, not production integration. Menu and drawer opening are real in the gallery; zoom values, release actions, panel contents, mobile behavior, focus management, and wiring to the tldraw editor are simulated. No live SystemSketch source was changed.

requirements.name: Calm default canvas
requirements.why: The current top-center release pill is distracting on a surface whose main job is spatial thinking.
requirements.passCondition: With all transient surfaces closed, utilities stay compact at the bottom-right and no release information floats over the upper canvas.

anchors.1: Release or utility chrome remains prominent in the main visual field.
anchors.3: The top is clear, but the bottom-right footprint or persistent panel is visually heavy.
anchors.5: The top is completely clear and the resting controls read as quiet whiteboard chrome.

requirements.name: Miro/FigJam familiarity
requirements.why: The design note explicitly prefers copying mature whiteboard conventions to avoid coherence work and relearning.
requirements.passCondition: A Miro or FigJam user can predict what the zoom, question-mark, and board-panel controls do from placement and form.

anchors.1: The controls use a novel layout or mental model unrelated to the references.
anchors.3: Individual icons are familiar, but composition or behavior diverges from the references.
anchors.5: Placement, grouping, and disclosure closely match a shown Miro or FigJam pattern.

requirements.name: Discoverable controls
requirements.why: Help, zoom, and the new right-side panel should be found without searching menus or remembering shortcuts.
requirements.passCondition: A first-time user can locate all three utilities from the resting canvas and tell which control opens the side panel.

anchors.1: Two or more utilities are hidden behind an unrelated control.
anchors.3: Every utility is reachable, but one requires menu exploration or an ambiguous icon.
anchors.5: All three utilities have visible, unambiguous affordances in the bottom-right.

requirements.name: Minimal custom code
requirements.why: SystemSketch currently keeps stock tldraw intact, and the project note names minimizing custom code as a goal.
requirements.passCondition: The direction can be built through supported tldraw UI component overrides plus a small host-owned status content component, without forking editor internals.

anchors.1: Requires a broad chrome rewrite or duplicated editor behavior.
anchors.3: Requires one meaningful owned navigation surface and some custom state/layout.
anchors.5: Mostly reuses the existing navigation surface and adds only narrow, isolated components.

requirements.name: Panel growth path
requirements.why: The placeholder should later become a useful Frames or board-overview surface without another navigation redesign.
requirements.passCondition: The panel has a stable launcher and an interaction container that can accept real board navigation content later.

anchors.1: The placeholder is a dead end or would need a new launcher later.
anchors.3: The panel can grow, but its current entry point is secondary or ambiguous.
anchors.5: The launcher and right-side container already express a durable board-navigation model.

hardGates.name: No top release overlay
hardGates.why: Removing the distracting upper-canvas status surface is the explicit user outcome.

hardGates.name: All three utilities reachable
hardGates.why: Help/status, zoom, and the placeholder panel are all part of the requested slice.

hardGates.name: No tldraw engine fork
hardGates.why: The editor and document model must remain upgradeable and stock beneath the owned chrome.

variants.name: FigJam Utility Strip
variants.thesis: Make the complete utility set one predictable segmented control: panel, zoom out, zoom value, zoom in, Help.
variants.bestWhen: You want the strongest zero-relearning match to the note's Figma-first decision and expect the right-side panel to become important.
variants.losesWhen: Preserving tldraw's existing navigation DOM and making the smallest first code change matters more than exact composition.

decisions.label: Composition
decisions.value: One FigJam-like five-part strip keeps every utility in a single visual grammar.

decisions.label: Help
decisions.value: A light popover opens above the question mark; SystemSketch status is the first section, followed by help links.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.value: The leftmost board-overview icon opens a fixed right drawer with a placeholder body.

decisions.label: Implementation seam
decisions.value: Own tldraw's supported NavigationPanel component, reuse editor zoom actions, and extract UpdatePill content into a reusable status section.

proof: The preview renders the same dotted board at 27% with no top release pill.
Help is open by default; click the question mark to close it, and click the leftmost icon to open the placeholder panel.

fr1.evidence: The resting state is one 212 px bottom-right strip and the entire upper canvas is clear.

fr2.evidence: The order, grouping, zoom percentage, and help placement directly reproduce the supplied FigJam bottom-right reference.

fr3.evidence: Panel, minus, zoom percentage, plus, and Help each have a persistent, separate target.

fr4.evidence: It fits the supported NavigationPanel seam but replaces that surface with an owned five-control composition and panel state.

fr5.evidence: The dedicated first control and fixed right drawer give board navigation a durable home.

g1.evidence: No SystemSketch element appears at the top of the mock.

g2.evidence: All three utilities have visible controls in the strip.

g3.evidence: The proposal uses public UI components and editor actions; no editor or store internals change.

variants.name: Miro Satellites
variants.thesis: Keep zoom, Help, and board overview as three small neighboring capsules rather than one owned mega-control.
variants.bestWhen: You want the smallest visual footprint and a conservative path that composes narrow components around tldraw's navigation behavior.
variants.losesWhen: A single coherent FigJam strip or an unmistakable panel launcher matters more than implementation modularity.

decisions.label: Composition
decisions.value: A Miro-like −/+ capsule and separate Help circle sit beside a small board-overview button.

decisions.label: Help
decisions.value: A dark Miro-style menu exposes status first and keeps support/navigation rows below.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.value: The board icon is independent, so the future Frames surface can evolve without changing zoom or Help.

decisions.label: Implementation seam
decisions.value: Use small supported overrides for NavigationPanel and HelpMenu; keep panel state in a sibling overlay.

proof: The preview keeps all three capsules in the bottom-right and no status at the top.
Help is open by default; the board icon independently opens the same placeholder panel.

fr1.evidence: Three small satellites leave the canvas quiet and avoid a long permanent strip.

fr2.evidence: The split −/+ and Help capsules plus dark menu closely match the supplied Miro references.

fr3.evidence: All utilities are visible, but the unlabeled board icon is less self-explanatory than a named rail or integrated pattern.

fr4.evidence: The composition can be split across narrow public UI overrides and a sibling drawer instead of one larger navigation rewrite.

fr5.evidence: The independent launcher can grow, but its visual relationship to the future panel is weak until opened.

g1.evidence: The mock has no top release element.

g2.evidence: Board icon, zoom capsule, and Help circle remain visible.

g3.evidence: The proposal stays within public UI override and editor-action seams.

variants.name: Progressive Help Hub
variants.thesis: Show only zoom and Help at rest; place the board-panel launcher and all SystemSketch status inside Help.
variants.bestWhen: Maximum canvas calm and the smallest code surface matter, while the board panel remains occasional rather than primary navigation.
variants.losesWhen: Users need to open the board panel often or must discover it without first exploring Help.

decisions.label: Composition
decisions.value: The resting chrome copies Miro's minimal −/+ and ? pair exactly.

decisions.label: Help
decisions.value: Help becomes a utility hub: status, panel entry, shortcuts, feedback, and support.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.value: A labeled Open board overview row inside Help launches the placeholder drawer.

decisions.label: Implementation seam
decisions.value: Keep navigation compact, enable an owned HelpMenu, and manage the drawer in the host overlay.

proof: The preview shows the smallest default chrome of the five directions.
Help is open by default; its labeled board-overview row launches the placeholder panel.

fr1.evidence: Only a 92 px zoom rocker and 42 px Help circle persist at rest.

fr2.evidence: The resting pair is directly Miro-like, but using Help as the panel launcher is not present in either reference.

fr3.evidence: Zoom and Help are obvious; the board panel is discoverable only after opening Help.

fr4.evidence: It can preserve a compact navigation component and concentrate new behavior in one HelpMenu plus one drawer.

fr5.evidence: The drawer can grow, but its launcher remains semantically nested under Help rather than board navigation.

g1.evidence: No status appears at the top of the board.

g2.evidence: Zoom and Help are visible; the labeled board-panel action is inside Help.

g3.evidence: All work stays in public HelpMenu/navigation overrides and a host drawer.

variants.name: Edge Navigator
variants.thesis: Give the future board panel a persistent vertical edge tab while zoom and Help remain a conventional bottom-right cluster.
variants.bestWhen: The Frames or board-overview panel is expected to become a frequent primary navigation surface.
variants.losesWhen: The panel stays occasional, or the always-visible edge tab feels too much like application chrome on a whiteboard.

decisions.label: Composition
decisions.value: Zoom and Help stay bottom-right; Board overview moves to a persistent right-edge tab.

decisions.label: Help
decisions.value: A compact popover contains release status and help actions without competing with panel navigation.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.value: The edge tab and drawer form one spatial object; opening the panel replaces the tab with a close control.

decisions.label: Implementation seam
decisions.value: Add one host-level edge overlay plus supported HelpMenu/navigation controls.

proof: The preview starts with the right panel open so its spatial relationship to the edge launcher is visible.
Close the panel to reveal the vertical Board tab; Help and zoom remain independent.

fr1.evidence: The top remains clear, but the persistent vertical edge tab adds a second chrome zone.

fr2.evidence: The bottom cluster is familiar, while a vertical board tab is closer to an IDE sidebar than the supplied whiteboard references.

fr3.evidence: The named Board tab makes the panel unmistakable, and zoom and Help remain visible.

fr4.evidence: It needs an additional responsive edge overlay and coordination with the existing right-side style panel.

fr5.evidence: A named, spatially attached edge launcher is a strong durable home for Frames and overview navigation.

g2.evidence: The edge launcher, zoom controls, and Help remain reachable.

g3.evidence: The edge overlay is host-owned and does not change editor internals.

variants.name: Shared Right Drawer
variants.thesis: Use one scalable right drawer for Help, SystemSketch status, and board overview, with tabs switching its purpose.
variants.bestWhen: You expect several utility surfaces and want one consistent responsive container instead of multiple popovers and panels.
variants.losesWhen: A quick Help click should stay lightweight, or strict fidelity to Miro/FigJam matters more than future consolidation.

decisions.label: Composition
decisions.value: Zoom stays a small strip; the status-dotted Help icon opens the shared right drawer.

decisions.label: Help
decisions.value: Help becomes a full drawer tab with the complete current release card and support actions.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.value: Board overview is a neighboring drawer tab rather than a separate overlay or launcher.

decisions.label: Implementation seam
decisions.value: Build one host-owned UtilityDrawer and let tldraw navigation/help triggers select its active tab.

proof: The preview opens the shared drawer on Help with the full status section visible.
Close it with × to inspect the calm bottom-right trigger; the Board overview tab remains visible in the drawer.

fr1.evidence: The resting state is quiet, but opening ordinary Help consumes a full-height right drawer.

fr2.evidence: The control placement is familiar, but Help-as-drawer and tabbed board navigation are not shown in the supplied references.

fr3.evidence: Zoom and Help are visible, while board overview becomes obvious only after the drawer opens.

fr4.evidence: One drawer simplifies overlay collisions later but requires new shared state, tabs, and responsive behavior now.

fr5.evidence: The shared full-height drawer is already a scalable container for overview, frames, and future utilities.

g1.evidence: No release status appears at the top.

g2.evidence: Zoom and Help are visible; board overview is a labeled drawer tab.

g3.evidence: The drawer is host UI and uses editor actions without changing the engine.
